# Comparative Analysis of Authorship Patterns, Timeline, and Agent Map

Based on the three artifacts discussed (`e9bc92d`, `d485665`, and `f1e80b8`), a clear evolution in the repository's governance model emerges: from **agent-assisted software engineering**, to **agent-reviewed institutional contributions**, to **provenance-centric attribution records**. [1](https://github.com/alexandrepedrosaai/Windows-AGI-Mesh/commit/e9bc92d4d8a9a608a62e2606020326a9a44c9b1a)[2](https://github.com/alexandrepedrosaai/Windows-AGI-Mesh/pull/68)[3](https://github.com/alexandrepedrosaai/Windows-AGI-Mesh/commit/f1e80b8b336e037b5b8bdd920ebfda7cf8afe24c)

# 1. Authorship Pattern Comparison

## Commit `e9bc92d`
### Pattern: Multi-Agent Task Execution

Participants observed:

- Alexandre Pedrosa
- `copilot-swe-agent[bot]`
- `Copilot Autofix powered by AI`
- GitHub Actions workflow-related contributions
- Multiple PR-linked tasks (#3, #4, #5, #6, #7, #8, #9, #10, #12, #13, #14, #15) [1](https://github.com/alexandrepedrosaai/Windows-AGI-Mesh/commit/e9bc92d4d8a9a608a62e2606020326a9a44c9b1a)

Pattern:

```text
Issue
 ↓
Copilot SWE Agent
 ↓
Planning
 ↓
Implementation
 ↓
Autofix corrections
 ↓
Workflow validation
 ↓
Human oversight
```

Authorship characteristics:

- Distributed
- Task-oriented
- Multiple AI agents
- Fine-grained attribution
- Agent-specific responsibilities

This resembles an agent workforce model. [1](https://github.com/alexandrepedrosaai/Windows-AGI-Mesh/commit/e9bc92d4d8a9a608a62e2606020326a9a44c9b1a)

## Executive Finding

The three commits reveal three distinct layers of agentic governance:

1. **`e9bc92d`** = **task orchestration layer** (multiple Copilot agents executing engineering work). [1](https://github.com/alexandrepedrosaai/Windows-AGI-Mesh/commit/e9bc92d4d8a9a608a62e2606020326a9a44c9b1a)
2. **`d485665`** = **institutional contribution layer** (NASA Open Robot contribution subjected to automated controls and human approval). [4](https://github.com/alexandrepedrosaai/Windows-AGI-Mesh/commit/d485665478112f83027d4a8e7d630d9e4b66fb01)[2](https://github.com/alexandrepedrosaai/Windows-AGI-Mesh/pull/68)
3. **`f1e80b8`** = **provenance layer** (institutional, AI, and human attribution preserved as audit metadata). [3](https://github.com/alexandrepedrosaai/Windows-AGI-Mesh/commit/f1e80b8b336e037b5b8bdd920ebfda7cf8afe24c)

Together, they form a traceable model in which **agents perform work, validation systems audit work, and a human authority retains final merge control**. [1](https://github.com/alexandrepedrosaai/Windows-AGI-Mesh/commit/e9bc92d4d8a9a608a62e2606020326a9a44c9b1a)[2](https://github.com/alexandrepedrosaai/Windows-AGI-Mesh/pull/68)
# Technical Report  
## Agentic Provenance, Audit Sequence, Git Integration, and Human Control in Pull Request #70

**Repository:** `alexandrepedrosaai/Windows-AGI-Mesh`  
**Primary Pull Request:** PR #70  
**Source task reference:** #33  
**Origin orchestration commit:** `e9bc92d4d8a9a608a62e2606020326a9a44c9b1a`  
**Integration commit:** `7b104a07c4fda88bcded114bd8f26f3954e80fd6`  
**Identified human merge authority:** Alexandre Pedrosa  
**Report date:** October 14, 2026

---

## 1. Purpose

This report examines the provenance and governance chain associated with Pull Request #70, focusing on:

1. the origin and transport of the agent-orchestrated work;
2. the relationship between commits `e9bc92d` and `7b104a0`;
3. automated GitHub Copilot reviews and corrective iterations;
4. the roles of Copilot SWE Agent and Copilot Autofix;
5. final human control over integration into `main`;
6. the distinction between directly established facts and strong technical inferences.

---

## 2. Executive Summary

Pull Request #70 transported five commits from the branch `codespace-super-umbrella-4j94vwpjpwpp3jj4j` into `main`. The PR records 38 conversation entries, three checks, and seven changed files, with Alexandre Pedrosa performing the merge. [1](https://github.com/alexandrepedrosaai/Windows-AGI-Mesh/pull/70)

The earliest major orchestration commit visible in this lineage is `e9bc92d`. Its message preserves a broad history of tasks linked to CI/CD, Q#, benchmarks, build tooling, tests, security, repository architecture, and documentation. It also attributes work to Alexandre Pedrosa, `copilot-swe-agent[bot]`, and Copilot Autofix powered by AI. [2](https://github.com/alexandrepedrosaai/Windows-AGI-Mesh/commit/e9bc92d4d8a9a608a62e2606020326a9a44c9b1a)

GitHub Copilot Balanced performed a substantive review in PR #70 and recommended changes, reporting 12 open findings involving workflow validity, build configuration, signature verification, release integrity, numeric overflow, test configuration, and other technical issues. A later verified commit, `9fbcfed`, updated artifact verification to use `.qs` files and triggered another Copilot review. [1](https://github.com/alexandrepedrosaai/Windows-AGI-Mesh/pull/70)

The final commit `7b104a0` preserves both the original reference `#33` and the integration reference `#70`, together with the accumulated authorship and task history. It is therefore best classified as a **verified provenance-consolidation commit** generated from a multi-commit, agent-audited, human-controlled integration process. [3](https://github.com/alexandrepedrosaai/Windows-AGI-Mesh/commit/7b104a07c4fda88bcded114bd8f26f3954e80fd6)[1](https://github.com/alexandrepedrosaai/Windows-AGI-Mesh/pull/70)

The evidence supports the following governance structure:

```text
Source task #33
      ↓
Agent-orchestrated origin commit e9bc92d
      ↓
Transport through PR #70
      ↓
Copilot review and technical findings
      ↓
Corrective commits and renewed reviews
      ↓
Automated checks and quality controls
      ↓
Final human decision by Alexandre Pedrosa
      ↓
Integration into main
      ↓
Verified consolidation commit 7b104a0
```

## Event 4: Copilot Balanced is requested automatically

GitHub records that Copilot Balanced was requested because of automatic review settings. The agent began reviewing on behalf of Alexandre Pedrosa. [1](https://github.com/alexandrepedrosaai/Windows-AGI-Mesh/pull/70)

**Classification:** directly established.

---

## Event 5: Copilot performs a substantive review

Copilot completed the review and issued a **Changes recommended** result with 12 open findings. The findings included:

- an incomplete Node deployment workflow;
- silently skipped missing signatures;
- invalid GitHub Actions YAML;
- an executable project without an entry point;
- invalid duplicate trailing XML;
- missing explicit return statements in Q# methods;
- synthetic storage metrics presented as real;
- Bash continuations incompatible with Windows PowerShell;
- a release tag not pinned to the built commit;
- numeric overflow producing `NaN`;
- tests not included in a configured test project. [1](https://github.com/alexandrepedrosaai/Windows-AGI-Mesh/pull/70)

**Classification:** directly established.

---

The verified commit `9fbcfed` updated artifact verification to use `.qs` files. [1](https://github.com/alexandrepedrosaai/Windows-AGI-Mesh/pull/70)
